venue.name: Jamie's Whaling Station & Adventure Centres - Tofino
venue.description: Jamie's Whaling Station & Adventure Centres runs wildlife boat tours from its own dock and marina at 606 Campbell Street in Tofino, and has a second location in Ucluelet. From Tofino the fleet runs whale watching, bear watching, sea otter, Hot Springs Cove, Meares Island Big Tree Trail, Freedom Cove and offshore pelagic trips, on covered cruisers carrying up to 45 passengers and on 12 passenger open zodiacs. Covered cruiser trips from Tofino are listed as all ages and take infants, while every zodiac passenger must be at least 4'8" (142cm) tall. The site publishes per person rates for every tour but no school or group rate.
venue.address: 606 Campbell St, Box 129, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0

facility_notes.washrooms: Depending on what vessel you are travelling on during your tour you may or may not have access to a washroom. Our larger vessels all have washrooms onboard for use. On our smaller vessels including our Zodiacs, we have small marine toilets that are for emergency use only.
facility_notes.bus_parking: In Tofino, we offer a large parking lot for our guests. This includes parking for RV motorhomes. All parking is FREE with your tour. The site describes guest and RV parking and does not mention bus parking.
facility_notes.rain_backup: Our tours are Rain or Shine and we ask that you check the forecast prior to arriving for your departure and dress accordingly. On occasion, if the sea conditions are too rough we will cancel or delay our departures.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Snacks and drinks are allowed on board the Tofino whale watching and sea otter vessels. Food and scented items are not allowed on bear watching tours. The site does not describe an indoor lunch space on shore.

restrictions: Anyone under the height of 4'8" (142cm) is also unable to join our Zodiac tours.
We do ask that any guest under the age of 19 travels with a supervising adult.
To ensure the safety for all on board, parents and guardians are responsible for the proper behavior of their children.
No running, jumping, screaming, or climbing railings is permitted.
For our bear watching tours, we ask that you do not bring any food or drinks other than water as bears have a strong sense of smell.
All tours are subject to the signing of a waiver releasing Jamie's Whaling Station from liability.
Hot Springs Cove Day Tour: Ages 0-2 are NOT permitted on tour.
We are happy to welcome certified and trained medical service or guide dogs on board our larger vessels (Lukwa/Stellar Sea). Emotional support or therapy dogs are not permitted on board.
venue.hours_notes: Check in is 30 minutes prior to your departure time. The site suggests allowing another 15 to 30 minutes after the tour to disembark, take off zodiac suits, use the washrooms and visit the gift shop. Exact departure times are shown on the online booking calendar rather than on the pages, and bear watching departures are set by the low tide.
venue.seasonal_notes: The 2026 whale watching season in Tofino runs from early February through October. Tofino bear watching runs April through October. Hot Springs Cove runs year round, and a separate set of fall and winter tours runs from the Tofino location from November to February.

programs.name: Tofino Covered Cruiser Whale Watching
programs.description: A 2.5 to 3 hour whale watching trip from the Tofino dock aboard a covered cruiser, with full commentary by a certified captain and naturalists. The site lists the tour as all ages: adults $200.34, youth 13 to 18 $179.14, children 3 to 12 $168.54, and infants 2 and under free. Grey whales are the whale most often seen, with Transient (Bigg's) Killer Whales and Humpback Whales also possible, along with sea lions, sea otters, seals and eagles. The same tour is also sold as a Tofino Whale & Bear Package, which pairs it with a bear watching trip on the same day or a different day.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in a heated indoor cabin with large windows, then move out to the open rear deck to watch for spouts, tails and breaching whales while a naturalist explains what is happening. Snacks and drinks are allowed on board, so they can eat and move between seats during the trip.
programs.our_note: This is the Tofino boat that takes babies and toddlers, and the one where children can get up, move around and eat. Check in is half an hour before the boat leaves and it takes a while to get everyone off afterwards, so block out closer to four hours than three.
programs.practical_summary: There is a toilet on the boat and washrooms at the Tofino station, parking is free, and the cabin is heated and covered. No indoor lunch space on shore and no group or school rate are published, so those are worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, $1 per person for research, rescue and education, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee if you book online.
programs.cancellation_note: Our Whale Watching tours have a 48-hour cancellation policy. If any cancellations are received, including a reduction in the passenger numbers, within 48 hours of the tour departure refunds will not be issued.
programs.evidence: Best for: little ones who need space to move around and have access to snacks

programs.name: Tofino Zodiac Whale Watching
programs.description: A 2.5 to 3 hour whale watching trip from Tofino on an open 12 passenger zodiac with forward facing seats and flotation suits provided. Every passenger must be at least 4'8" (142cm) tall, and the site does not recommend the tour for anyone pregnant or with back, neck or knee problems, osteoporosis, incontinence, recent surgery or limited mobility. Rates are adults $179.14, youth 13 to 18 $157.94 and children 12 and under $147.34, and a private zodiac for up to 12 people is $2,703. There is only an emergency marine toilet on board.
programs.what_children_do: Zip into a full body flotation suit at the station, sit strapped into a forward facing seat on an open boat, and hold on through a fast, bouncy ride out to where the whales feed.
programs.our_note: The height rule rules out most children under about eleven or twelve, so measure before you plan anything around this. Everyone stays seated for the whole trip and the toilet on board is for emergencies only.
programs.practical_summary: Free parking and washrooms at the Tofino station, but nothing usable on the water and no shelter from rain or spray. The height rule is the thing to settle first, and no group or school rate is published.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, $1 per person for research, rescue and education, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee if you book online.
programs.cancellation_note: Our Whale Watching tours have a 48-hour cancellation policy. If any cancellations are received, including a reduction in the passenger numbers, within 48 hours of the tour departure refunds will not be issued.
programs.evidence: Anyone under the height of 4’8″ (142cm) is also unable to join our Zodiac tours.

programs.name: Tofino Cruiser Bear Watching
programs.description: A 2.5 to 3 hour black bear watching trip from Tofino on the Stellar Sea, a fully covered panoramic view cruiser with interior bench seating and an onboard washroom. The boat departs daily at low tide and travels through Browning Pass to the shoreline of Fortune Channel, where bears forage for crabs and clams. The site lists the tour as all ages: adults $200.34, youth 13 to 18 $179.14 and children 3 to 12 $168.54. No food or scented items are allowed on board and voices must stay at a whisper. The site notes that in 2027 this tour will be 2.5 hours in duration.
programs.what_children_do: Sit on a bench in a covered cabin with panoramic windows that open, keep their voices to a whisper, and watch the rocky shoreline for black bears turning over rocks. The crew says when it is safe to stand up and stretch.
programs.our_note: No food, no scented things and whispers only for the whole trip, which is a lot to ask of a three year old for three hours. Departure follows the low tide, so the time moves day to day and may land mid nap.
programs.practical_summary: One toilet on board, free parking and a fully covered cabin, so rain is not a problem. Snacks are not allowed at all on this one and no group or school rate is published.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, $1 per person for research, rescue and education, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee if you book online.
programs.cancellation_note: Our Bear Watching tours have a 48-hour cancellation policy. If any cancellations are received, including a reduction in the passenger numbers, within 48 hours of the tour departure refunds will not be issued.
programs.evidence: little ones who are good at staying in their seat for long periods, do not need snacks

programs.name: Tofino Zodiac Bear Watching
programs.description: A 2.5 to 3 hour black bear watching trip from Tofino on an open 12 passenger zodiac, departing daily at low tide for Browning Pass and Fortune Channel. Every passenger must be at least 4'8" (142cm) tall and the site does not recommend the tour for anyone pregnant or with back, neck or knee problems, osteoporosis, incontinence, recent surgery or limited mobility. Rates are adults $179.14, youth 13 to 18 $157.94 and children 12 and under $147.34, with a private zodiac for up to 12 people at $2,703. The site states that Zodiac Bear Watching Tours in Tofino operate on a limited basis.
programs.what_children_do: Put on a full body flotation suit, sit strapped into an open boat for a fast ride into calm inlet waters, then sit still and quiet while the boat idles near the shore to watch bears forage.
programs.our_note: The height rule rules out most young children, and the site says these zodiac bear trips only run on a limited basis, so do not build a day around one without confirming it is running. The covered boat does the same route with a washroom and a roof.
programs.practical_summary: Free parking and washrooms at the Tofino station, and only an emergency toilet on the boat. Availability is limited and the height rule applies, so confirm both before you plan anything.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, $1 per person for research, rescue and education, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee if you book online.
programs.cancellation_note: Our Bear Watching tours have a 48-hour cancellation policy. If any cancellations are received, including a reduction in the passenger numbers, within 48 hours of the tour departure refunds will not be issued.
programs.evidence: Anyone under the height of 4’8″ (142cm) is also unable to join our Zodiac tours.

programs.name: Tofino Otters and Inlets Tour
programs.description: A 1.5 to 2 hour trip through the calm inlet waters around Tofino looking for sea otters, with commentary from a certified captain and naturalists. The site lists the tour as all ages: adults $147.34, youth 13 to 18 $126.14, children 3 to 12 $115.54, and an infant rate for ages 2 and under. The vessel has an interior cabin with bench seating, an open rear deck and a marine toilet, snacks and drinks are allowed, and the site says outside voices are ok. Sightings are mainly sea otters, with birds, seals and sea lions also possible.
programs.what_children_do: Sit on a bench in a heated cabin or stand at the rear deck in calm inlet water, watching for sea otters floating on their backs. They can talk at a normal volume, eat their snacks, and stretch their legs when the crew says it is safe.
programs.our_note: This is the shortest and calmest Tofino trip and the only one where the site says normal talking volume is fine, which makes it the easiest first boat for under fives. Bring books and small toys, because the site suggests it.
programs.practical_summary: A toilet on board, snacks allowed, calm water and about two hours on the water. The months it runs are not published anywhere, so check the booking calendar before you plan a date.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, $1 per person for research, rescue and education, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee if you book online.
programs.cancellation_note: Our Otters & Inlets tours have a 48-hour cancellation policy. If any cancellations are received, including a reduction in the passenger numbers, within 48 hours of the tour departure refunds will not be issued.
programs.evidence: little ones who need a shorter time out on the water and access to snacks.

programs.name: Hot Springs Cove Day Tour
programs.description: A 6 to 6.5 hour day trip from Tofino to Maquinna Provincial Park on a cruiser style vessel, roughly 26 nautical miles each way and 1 to 1.5 hours of travel in each direction. On arrival there is a 30 to 40 minute boardwalk hike through rainforest to natural thermal pools, where guests soak for a couple of hours. The site lists ages 3 and up, with ages 0 to 2 not permitted, and one flat rate of $265 for every age bracket. A private tour for up to 12 people is $5,406. The tour runs year round with one daily morning departure whose time varies through the year.
programs.what_children_do: Ride an hour or more each way in a heated cabin watching for whales, eagles and sea lions, then walk a 30 to 40 minute boardwalk trail through rainforest and sit in warm natural rock pools before walking back.
programs.our_note: Six and a half hours with a rainforest walk at each end makes this a long day for small legs, and children under three are not allowed at all. You have to carry in a full lunch and every drink, because there is no drinking water out there.
programs.practical_summary: A washroom on the boat, free parking at the station, and a long day with a real hike in the middle. Bring lunch, water in something other than glass, swimsuits, towels and shoes that can get wet.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, $1 per person for research, rescue and education, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee if you book online.
programs.evidence: Ages 0-2 are NOT permitted on tour

programs.name: Big Tree Trail - Meares Island
programs.description: A boat drop off from Tofino to the Big Tree trailhead on Meares Island, where guests walk the 1.2 km wooden boardwalk through old growth rainforest on their own. The site lists the tour as all ages and 1.5 to 3 hours, with adults $37.10, youth 13 to 18 $31.80, children 4 to 12 $26.50, and an infant rate for ages 3 and under. Hiking the boardwalk briskly takes about 40 minutes, most guests spend 1 to 1.5 hours, and a full 4 km natural loop beyond the boardwalk adds about 1.5 hours. The crossing is made by zodiac, dogs are not permitted, and the site notes the boardwalk is split logs that may be soft, slippery or missing.
programs.what_children_do: Cross by boat, then walk a narrow wooden boardwalk of split logs through old growth forest, looking up at cedars six metres across, and turn back whenever they have had enough.
programs.our_note: Nobody guides you once you land, so an adult has to set the pace and decide how far to go. The crossing is by zodiac and the site does not say whether the zodiac height rule applies here, which is the first thing to ask.
programs.practical_summary: Cheapest of the Tofino trips and the only self guided one, but the boardwalk has no railings described, no washroom on the island and boards that can be soft or missing. Not recommended for anyone using a mobility aid, and strollers are not mentioned at all.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, $1 per person for research, rescue and education, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee if you book online. The Big Tree Trail is not part of the multi tour discount.
programs.evidence: This tour is self guided and is not recommended for those with limited mobility or those who use a mobility aid

programs.name: Freedom Cove - Floating Gardens
programs.description: A 2.5 hour trip from Tofino by open zodiac around Meares Island to Freedom Cove, a floating off grid home and garden built from 1992 across twelve connecting platforms, with greenhouses, an art gallery, a dance floor and a lighthouse. The resident artists host the tour. The site lists the tour as all ages but states that ages 12 and under must be at least 4'8" (142cm) tall, with adults $147.34, youth 13 to 18 $136.74 and children 4 to 12 $126.14. The site says to call Jamie's Whaling Station to book this tour.
programs.what_children_do: Ride an open zodiac through calm inlet water, then step onto floating platforms and walk through greenhouses, a garden and an art gallery while the people who built and live there explain how it works.
programs.our_note: Children twelve and under still have to clear the zodiac height rule, so this is not one for a preschool group. Booking is by phone rather than through the website calendar.
programs.practical_summary: An open boat with no washroom for the crossing and no shelter from rain, and a height rule that rules out most young children. Call the Tofino office to book and to ask what is on site once you arrive.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, $1 per person for research, rescue and education, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee if you book online.
programs.evidence: Ages 12 and under must be at least 4'8"/142cm in height

programs.name: Tofino Pelagic Wildlife Tour
programs.description: A 6 to 7 hour offshore trip from the Tofino dock, travelling up to 25 nautical miles out towards the continental shelf on an open 12 passenger zodiac, looking for pelagic birds such as black footed albatross, shearwaters and storm petrels along with humpback and fin whales, dolphins, porpoise and fur seals. One flat rate of $349 per person. The site lists the tour as all ages but states that ages 12 and under must be at least 4'8" (142cm) tall, and says guests requiring frequent bathroom visits are not suited to this tour.
programs.what_children_do: Sit strapped into an open zodiac in a flotation suit, gloves and a toque for a long run offshore, scanning open water and sky for seabirds and whales.
programs.our_note: Six or seven hours on an open boat far offshore with only an emergency toilet is not a children's group outing, and the height rule rules out most under twelves anyway. Listed here so it is not mistaken for a family trip.
programs.practical_summary: No shelter, no usable washroom and a very long day on open water. The height rule applies to everyone twelve and under.
programs.extra_fees_note: On top of the listed rates, checkout adds 5% GST, a $2 port fee, $1 per person for research, rescue and education, a $5 fuel surcharge, and a 6% booking fee if you book online.
programs.evidence: Anyone under the height of 4’8″ (142cm) is also unable to join our Zodiac tours.

programs.name: Private Tour
programs.description: A customisable private charter departing from Tofino or Ucluelet on any vessel in the fleet, booked through an inquiry form rather than the online calendar. The site lists the tour as all ages with a customisable duration, and says rates start at $850 per hour plus taxes and fees with a two hour minimum, depending on which vessel is chosen. The Lukwa can host up to 45 passengers, and the form offers passenger bands of 1 to 12, 13 to 30 and 31 to 45. Published options include a whale and bear combo, bird watching, a remote picnic on a landing craft with catered lunch on request, and a sunset cruise.
programs.our_note: This is the only route on the site that fits a whole group on one boat with a schedule you choose, so it is the one to ask about for a class. The form asks for a date, a departure town and a passenger count, and the reply comes back with a quote.
programs.practical_summary: Rates start at $850 an hour with a two hour minimum, so the cost per child depends entirely on how many come. Nothing about children's groups, chaperone numbers or lunch arrangements is published, so ask all of it in the inquiry.
programs.extra_fees_note: Rates start at $850 per hour plus taxes and fees, with a two hour minimum, and vary by vessel.
programs.evidence: Our rates start at $850 per hour plus taxes and fees (2 hour minimum) depending on choice of vessel.
